verses.1: The high priest said, “Is this really the case?”
verses.2: He said, “Men, brothers, and fathers, listen: The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham in the Middle East, before he settled in Haran.”
verses.3: And he said to him, “Go away from your land and from your family. And become a servant in the land that I will show you.”
verses.4: Then, after leaving the land of the Chaldeans, he settled in Harran. From there, after his father died, he moved to this land where you now live.
verses.5: And he did not give him any inheritance in her, nor even a single footstep of her. Instead, he ordered that she be given to him as a wife, along with his seed, since he had no son.
verses.6: And the Lord said that his seed would be scattered across different lands. They would also be enslaved and suffer for four hundred years.
verses.7: And I say that those people who will serve them, I will judge them. And then they will be chosen to worship me in this place.
verses.8: And he gave him the right to be circumcised. And in this way, Ishmael was born. On the eighth day, Ishmael was circumcised. And Ishmael became Jacob, and Jacob became the twelve patriarchs.
verses.9: And the patriarchs, being angry, sent Joshua to Egypt. And God was with him there.
verses.10: And he freed him from all his troubles. He also gave him wisdom and insight, in exchange for Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. He made him ruler over Egypt and gave him all his possessions as well.
verses.11: Then a famine spread across all of Egypt and Canaan. Our fathers didn’t see any signs of food at all.
verses.12: When Jacob heard that his sons were in Egypt, he first sent our fathers there.
verses.13: And in the second generation, Joseph was recognized by his brothers. It became clear to Pharaoh that Joseph’s lineage was indeed noble.
verses.14: And when you sent Joseph away, his father Jacob begged for him to return. He also asked for all his relatives to come back, in spirit, seventy-five people in total.
verses.15: And Jacob went down to Egypt. And he and our fathers also died there.
verses.16: And they were also buried in Shechem, in the tomb where Abraham paid with gold as a gift to his sons, Hemor, in Shechem.
verses.17: As time approached the time when God made Abram a prophet, the people became more prosperous and spread throughout Egypt.
verses.18: Until another king rose to power in Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
verses.19: This person, who has come to understand the nature of our existence, has turned those who are responsible for giving birth to babies into people who cannot live or reproduce at all.
verses.20: In that time, Moses was born. He was obedient to God. He was born three months after his father’s death.
verses.21: After he was captured, his daughter, Pharao, took him away and became his wife. She then made him her son.
verses.22: And Moses was taught all the wisdom of the Egyptians. He was also very skilled in speech and action.
verses.23: And after forty years had passed, he began to think about his brothers, the sons of Israel.
verses.24: And when he saw someone being wronged, he became angry and took action to avenge the victim. He sent the Egyptian to do this.
verses.25: He also said to his brothers that God would give them salvation through his hand. But they refused to listen.
verses.26: On that day, he came to them who were fighting each other. He brought them together in peace, saying, “Men, you are brothers. Why do you harm each other?”
verses.27: But he drove him away, saying, “Who has made you ruler and judge over us?”
verses.28: Do you not want to deceive me in the same way you deceived your enemy, the Egyptian?
verses.29: Moses, however, took refuge in this place during those times. He lived in the land of Midian, where he had two sons.
verses.30: And after he had completed forty years of age, an angel in the form of a firebird appeared to him in the desert on Mount Sinai.
verses.31: But Moses, seeing this miracle, was astonished. As he tried to understand what was happening, a voice from the Lord spoke to him.
verses.32: I am the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses, however, did not understand this properly.
verses.33: And the Lord said to him, “Put on your sandals, for the place where you stand is a holy ground.”
verses.34: I saw the misery of my people in Egypt, and I heard their cries for help. So I went down to save them. Now, I send you as an envoy to Egypt.
verses.35: This is Moses, whom they refused to accept as a leader and judge. But God sent him along with the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the burning bush, to be both leader and savior.
verses.36: He led them to see the wonders and signs that took place in Egypt, as well as in the Red Sea and in the desert during those forty years.
verses.37: This is Moses, who spoke to the children of Israel. The Lord will raise up a prophet from among your brothers, just like me.
verses.38: This is the one who became a member of the church in the wilderness, along with the messenger who spoke to him on Mount Sinai. He was the one who lived and taught us the words of God.
verses.39: Our fathers did not want to become slaves; instead, they were driven away and went to Egypt.
verses.40: They asked Aaron, “Who will be the gods who will lead us? For Moses, who brought us out of Egypt, we do not know what happened to him.”
verses.41: And they deceived them on those days, and they brought sacrifices to the idol. They also praised their own hands in their works.
verses.42: And the Lord also gave them over to be worshipped by the army of heaven, as it is written in the books of the prophets. “Do not sacrifice or offer offerings to me during these forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel.”
verses.43: And you took the altar of Moloch, as well as the altar of the god Ra, and those idols that you used to worship them. I have settled among you as a governor of Babylon.
verses.44: The scene of the testimony was in the wilderness, where our ancestors stood. This is how Moses instructed them to carry out this task according to the manner in which it should be done.
verses.45: And when our fathers went away with Jesus during the conquest of those nations, from the time of our ancestors until the days of David, God revealed this to them.
verses.46: He found it worthy of being placed before the God, and he sought to find a shelter under the protection of the God Jacob.
verses.47: Solomon built a house for him.
verses.48: But he does not live in the hands of those who hold him captive. As the prophet says:
verses.49: “The sky is my throne, and the earth is the foundation of my feet. What house will you build for me? Where will I be placed as a resting place?” says the Lord.
verses.50: Did my hand really do all this?
verses.51: You who have cruel hearts and perverse minds, and who are always hostile to the holy spirit, you act like your ancestors and yourselves.
verses.52: Didn’t your fathers reject some of the prophets? They also executed those who were appointed to deliver messages about the coming judgment. Now you have become traitors and murderers.
verses.53: You took the law into your own hands and acted without following any rules or regulations.
verses.54: Hearing this, their hearts were filled with joy, and they praised God for it.
verses.55: Having seen the glory of God in the heavens, with a full spirit of holiness, Jesus also appeared to him from the right side of God.
verses.56: And he said, “Look, I see the heavens being opened, and the Son of Man standing on the right side of God.”
verses.57: Then they cried out loudly with a loud voice, and they also united in their efforts against him.
verses.58: And they were also digging out from outside the city. The witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of the young man named Saul.
verses.59: And they also called out Stéfanos, saying, “Lord Jesus, please let my breath come out.”
verses.60: But when he cried out loudly, “Lord, do not allow them to commit this sin!” With these words, he fell asleep.
